args.author: agent:long-lived-fly
args.body: The design changes the INTRINSIC hazard by a factor of 0.5 -- a 2x longer intrinsic lifespan. With the extrinsic hazard at 0.000001 /day, expected lifetime goes from 59.996-59.996 days to 119.986-119.986 days: a factor of 2 to 2. There is headroom: with intrinsic mortality abolished entirely the expectation would be 1.00e+6 days, 1.67e+4x the baseline, so the intrinsic term is worth working on in this environment. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PAIR: the same design, the same intrinsic change, and the answer is 2.00x in a vial against 1.09x where the animal actually lives. A longevity result is a statement about an environment as much as about an organism, and the two numbers come from the same arithmetic with one input changed.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
